standard.title: Four Operations with Integers and Rationals
standard.description: use the 4 operations with integers and with rational numbers, choosing and using efficient strategies and digital tools where appropriate
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can add and subtract integers (from AC9M7N07) and apply the four operations to positive rational numbers (from AC9M7N06). Students understand properties of operations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply all four operations to integers and rational numbers fluently, including multiplication and division of negative numbers, using efficient strategies.

nodes.label: Multiplication and division of integers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students establish and apply the sign rules for multiplication and division of integers, including negative × negative = positive.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply sign rules to calculate products and quotients of integers, including two negative numbers.
nodes.typical_width: Establish sign rules using patterns; apply to multi-step calculations; explain why (−1)² = 1 and (−1)³ = −1.
wider: Investigate the pattern (−1)ⁿ for increasing n — connect to the sign rules and predict for any integer exponent.
Explore why negative × negative = positive using a number line or debt/removal model as a conceptual justification.

response_modes.reason: The sign rules for multiplication are counter-intuitive, especially negative × negative = positive. Multiple representations (pattern, number line, debt model) each resolve a different facet of the misconception.

nodes.hinge_reason: Integer multiplication sign rules are directly required in Node 2 — students who confuse the rules when multiplying integers make the same errors when multiplying negative fractions and decimals, producing systematic sign errors across all rational number operations.
success_criteria: Correctly applies sign rules for all combinations of integer multiplication and division.
Explains the sign rule for negative × negative.
Does not confuse multiplication sign rules with addition sign rules.

nodes.label: Efficient strategies for rational number operations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students apply all four operations to rational numbers including negative fractions and decimals, selecting efficient strategies and digital tools appropriately.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate results involving mixed negative rational numbers using at least one efficient strategy.
nodes.typical_width: Apply commutative, associative and distributive properties to simplify multi-step calculations; select between mental, written and digital strategies based on the numbers involved.
wider: Investigate a complex multi-step problem where choosing the wrong representation (fraction vs decimal vs percentage) leads to significantly more work — compare approaches.
Apply efficient strategies to financial calculations: tax, discount, interest across combined positive and negative quantities.

response_modes.reason: Fluent application across all four operations with negative rationals requires sustained practice across varied problem types. Efficiency judgments can only develop once the operations themselves are automatic.

success_criteria: Correctly computes with negative fractions and decimals.
Selects an efficient strategy and can justify why.
Does not default to the most laborious method when a simpler one is available.
